title: Lindt Opens Its First-Ever India Store in New Delhi's Aerocity
excerpt: The Swiss chocolatier's 1,100 sq ft Worldmark boutique features a 25-flavour LINDOR Pick & Mix bar, live chocolatiers and festive gifting ranges — a first for the brand in India.
body:
• Swiss chocolatier Lindt & Sprüngli opened its first-ever retail store in India at Worldmark, Aerocity, New Delhi, on September 4, 2026 — an 1,100 sq ft boutique.
  • The flagship feature is the LINDOR 'Pick & Mix' experience: more than 25 truffle flavours, a grab-a-bag fill-your-own format and floor-to-ceiling foil-wall displays of milk, dark, coconut, hazelnut and sea salt varieties.
  • The range spans LINDOR, EXCELLENCE premium dark slabs, EXTRA CREAMY, the newly launched Choco Wafer range, pralines, live chocolatiers, tastings, personalised gifting and seasonal hampers.
  • Until now Lindt was available in India only via gourmet stores, online and duty-free. Fellow Swiss brand Läderach entered Delhi back in August 2023.

Lindt lovers in India no longer need to wait for a duty-free run. Lindt & Sprüngli has opened its first-ever retail store in the country — an 1,100 sq ft boutique at Worldmark, Aerocity, New Delhi, which opened its doors on September 4.

The Pick & Mix experience

The store's centrepiece is the LINDOR 'Pick & Mix' experience: more than 25 truffle flavours — some exclusive to the store — in a grab-a-bag, fill-your-own format, set against floor-to-ceiling foil-wall displays spanning milk, dark, coconut, hazelnut, sea salt and wafer varieties. Live chocolatiers pour moulds in-store, trained "chocolate advisors" guide tastings, and the boutique carries personalised gifting collections, hampers, seasonal launches and baking products alongside the LINDOR, EXCELLENCE, EXTRA CREAMY and newly launched Choco Wafer ranges.

"Opening our very first Lindt store in India marks an important milestone for us. Lindt chocolate is about creating moments of indulgence... We want to enchant the consumers of India with chocolate."

— Dr Adalbert Lechner, CEO, Lindt & Sprüngli

Why Aerocity, why now

The Aerocity location is deliberate: the hospitality and business district next to the international airport draws locals, travellers and corporate gift shoppers alike — and its World St food promenade is fast becoming a launchpad for global brands, hosting Olive Garden and Time Out Market's first India outlet. Lindt, which runs some 650 own stores worldwide and reported CHF 5.92 billion in sales in 2025, is betting that India's premium chocolate market is ready for a flagship presence. Globally, the company reaches consumers through its own stores plus roughly 100 distributor partners; India, until now, sat firmly in the latter camp.

Background: the Swiss chocolate race

Lindt is not the first Swiss chocolatier to plant a flag in the capital. Läderach opened at DLF Emporio in August 2023 and has since expanded to Mumbai's Jio World Plaza. But Lindt's brand recognition in India runs deeper — built over decades through gourmet retail, online channels and suitcases carried home from abroad — giving the new boutique an instant audience.

What's next

The festive season will be the first real test: with Diwali weeks away, the boutique's gifting and hamper ranges are timed for peak demand. For Indian chocolate lovers, the bigger question is whether Aerocity is a one-off flagship or the first of a national rollout. Lindt has not disclosed India pricing or expansion plans — global expansion has typically followed the flagship model, but with the festive season arriving in weeks, the company's immediate focus will be on proving demand for premium chocolate retail in the capital.
